دَائِصٌ A thief: pl. دَاصَةٌ. (S, K.) ―
-b2- One who follows the magistrates, and goes round about a thing. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ―
-b3- The pl., mentioned above, also signifies Men who flee from war, or battle: or who put themselves in motion for flight. (TA.) ―
-b4- And The lowest or basest or meanest sort of mankind, or of people; because of their being much in commotion: (Kr, M:) one of such is termed دَائِصٌ. (M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
